root_cause: The reducer gate is strict > with an inter-author tie-breaker (event.updatedBy < existing.updatedBy). When the same actor edits the same task twice within one wall-clock second, both events get the same Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) timestamp, and the same updatedBy — so the tie-break (lower pubkey wins) evaluates false for identical pubkeys, and the second event is silently dropped. This affects the optimistic apply in dispatch() AND every receiver, since the bumped timestamp is embedded in the published rumor.
fix_description: Approach B (sender-side monotonic clock) with sub-frame re-entrancy guard. (1) Added pure helper ensureMonotonicTimestamp(event, existing) in src/store/task-store-utils.ts: for the four mutation types, if event.updatedAt <= existing.updatedAt, returns a new event with updatedAt = existing.updatedAt + 1. (2) In dispatch() (task-store.tsx), called before both the optimistic setState and the rumor publish so receivers also get the bumped timestamp. (3) Added synchronous stateRef.current = nextState immediately after setState(nextState) and before the first await — without this, two dispatch() calls within the same render frame both read the stale updatedAt from the previous React render cycle, both bump to T+1, and the reducer drops the second. task.created is exempt (FWW).

VQ1.question: New deterministic unit test proves two same-actor edits with equal/non-increasing timestamps converge to the LAST edit, and it fails pre-fix?
VQ1.answer: YES. Three reducer-level tests in task-reducer.test.ts compose applyEvent + ensureMonotonicTimestamp + the mutable-ref pattern directly: (1) 'documents the raw-reducer drop' — applyEvent with no bump asserts second edit rejected (pins why bump is needed). (2) 'monotonic bump restores convergence' — ensureMonotonicTimestamp + applyEvent asserts last edit wins (T+1). (3) 'sub-frame burst' — simulates two dispatch() read-modify-write loops with synchronous ref advance, asserts T→T+1→T+2 and second edit's value wins; fails without the stateRef advance. Tests (2) and (3) both fail pre-fix (import error or wrong final state) and pass post-fix.
VQ1.evidence: npx vitest run src/store/task-reducer.test.ts — 15 passed. 'sub-frame burst' would produce status=in_progress at T+1 (second dispatch dropped) without the stateRef advance; passes as done at T+2 with it.

VQ2.question: Fix addresses root cause (coarse ordering key), NOT a symptom (not just rewriting e2e timestamps / test special-casing)?
VQ2.answer: YES. The fix is in dispatch(), the single chokepoint through which all task mutations flow. It addresses the ordering key problem directly: ensures that the LWW gate always sees strictly increasing timestamps for sequential same-actor edits. No e2e specs were modified, no producer timestamps were changed.
VQ2.evidence: Files changed: task-store-utils.ts, task-store.tsx, task-store.monotonic.test.ts, docs/task-protocol.md. Board.tsx, task-events.ts, and all e2e specs are untouched.

VQ5.question: Fix composes with the forthcoming updatedByDevice clientId tie-break (targets ordering axis, leaves the concurrent-tie axis free)?
VQ5.answer: YES. ensureMonotonicTimestamp operates only on the timestamp ordering axis: it bumps updatedAt when it would fail the strict > gate. It does not touch updatedBy or any hypothetical updatedByDevice field. The reducer's existing updatedBy tie-breaker is untouched and the forthcoming device tie-break sits below it in the same gate — neither is preempted or blocked by this change. The synchronous stateRef advance likewise only affects the ordering axis (ensures the second dispatch reads the post-first-apply state); it does not touch the tie-break dimensions. For concurrent inter-author edits, each actor's dispatch() has its own stateRef.current; both bump independently; the updatedBy tie-breaker resolves convergently.
VQ5.evidence: task-reducer.ts unchanged. Concurrent-tie tested in task-store.monotonic.test.ts ('bumps inter-author tie too'). Sub-frame burst tested in task-reducer.test.ts ('sub-frame burst').

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The main friction was that task-store.tsx cannot be imported directly in vitest (Vite's define plugin transforms process.env in a way that breaks the test environment). The solution — extracting the helper to a dependency-free task-store-utils.ts — is actually cleaner, but the failure mode (AggregateError: oxc transform error) was opaque and required a diagnostic step.
retrospective.surprised_by: The existing TypeScript errors in the e2e test files (missing updatedBy on hand-crafted Task objects) were not caused by this fix — they predate it. Worth noting since they could confuse a future tsc run.
